chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about leasing (ijarah), and he said: 'It is sound, there is no objection to it, if he is sincere to the extent of his capacity. Moses (peace be upon him) leased himself and stipulated, saying: 'If I will, eight years; if I will, ten.' Then Allah, Exalted and Mighty, revealed concerning him: "[I will marry you to] the best of ten years, if you complete eight."' (Quran 28:27-28)

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: There is no contradiction between the two reports because the first report is construed as indicating a type of dislike (karahah) rather than prohibition (haram). The reason for this dislike is that one cannot be certain that the employee will not be sincere in his work, thus becoming deserving of blame. And he drew attention to this in the second report by his saying: 'No objection to it if he is sincere to the extent of his capacity.'

key_terms.ثَمَانِيَ حِجَجٍ: Eight years (referring to the duration of Moses' lease)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on employment contracts (ijarah) in Shia Islam and what is the significance of Moses' lease?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* to validate *ijarah* by citing Prophet Moses (AS) as a precedent, while noting the scholarly distinction that the contract is merely disliked (*karahat*) rather than prohibited if the employee lacks full sincerity. The text emphasizes that validity hinges on the employee exerting their best effort (*nasaq*), a condition highlighted by the narrator Muhammad ibn al-Hasan to reconcile differing reports.
